quote: The world stands out on either side / No wider than the heart is wide; / Above the world is stretched the sky,— / No higher than the soul is high.
source: Edna St. Vincent Millay, Renascence, the closing verse paragraph, lines 1 to 4, Renascence and Other Poems (Mitchell Kennerley, 1917)

evidence.where: Project Gutenberg ebook 109, the full text of Renascence and Other Poems, plus a second full-text posting of the 1917 volume
evidence.edition: Renascence and Other Poems (New York: Mitchell Kennerley, 1917)
evidence.locator: Renascence, the closing verse paragraph of twelve lines, its first four

reason: The four lines stand word for word in the 1917 text, including the comma and dash after sky. The locator is sharpened to say lines 1 to 4 of that paragraph, because the paragraph runs eight lines further and a reader should not expect these to be the last words of the poem.
